_: Writes data/side_stories.json: the side stories Tom approved (Guide 11 #20-26,

lines.text: Three small crystal babies are tumbling over each other at Catkins' feet, chiming like wind bells.
Coldy's little ones followed her down the mountain. They're not cursed any more, just loud. They need names. Real ones; 'Oi, you' doesn't count.

steps.hint: The crystal babies have names. Come back to Catkins tomorrow.

lines.text: They want to help. Guard the meadow, chase off Grumps, show off. Mostly show off.
Crystals grow strong on light. Bring me two Light Motes and I'll teach them to shine on purpose.

ask.text: Two Light Motes. The deep floors of the mine shed them, and the moon has a few lying about.

steps.hint: Bring Catkins 2 Light Motes for the crystal babies.

lines.text: The babies line up in a row, glowing steadily, almost serious. One of them hiccups a spark.
They'll stand with you now, when there's fighting to be done. Little helpers with big hearts. Like someone else I know.
Heart at the chest. They learned that first. I didn't teach them; they watched you.
Your big friend, the penguin who doesn't fight. Years back, one just like him came through the quarry. Bigger, if you can believe it. Asked the way to the highlands.
Said he was going to find where the sky starts. Left a fish on my desk as thanks. I didn't have the heart to say I don't eat fish.

steps.hint: Granite saw a huge penguin head for the highlands years ago. Ask Big Jim's friends in town: Sel reads old marks.

lines.text: A penguin carving? Above the quarry's top shelf there's a mark nobody's read. Webbed feet, a fire, an arrow pointing up.
Bring me five stone so I can make a rubbing board, and I'll tell you what it says.

ask.text: Five stone. For the rubbing board. Science is mostly carrying things.

steps.hint: Bring Sel 5 Stone to read the penguin carving.

lines.text: It says: 'Gone to see the sky. Tell Jim the fire's still lit.' And under it, a little drawing of a cave mouth, high up, behind a waterfall on Mount Prismatica.
Somebody waited a long time for somebody to read that. Go and tell Big Jim. Then, if I were you, I'd go and look for a waterfall.

steps.hint: Tell Big Jim his brother's message. The cave is behind a waterfall high on Mount Prismatica.

lines.text: Odd thing. The oldest town plans show a little room under the hall. A vault, with a lock drawn like a snowflake. Nobody's had a key in living memory.
Your friend Coldy wears a key like a snowflake. I'm a mayor, not a detective, but I can count to two.

steps.hint: Alder thinks Coldy's sacred key fits a vault under the town hall. Theo keeps the old records.

lines.text: The vault! There's a note in the founders' ledger: 'Sealed by the cold folk of the mountain, to keep what the town will need when it forgets.'
The ledger's water-stained. An old coin was pressed in the page as a bookmark, the same mint as the vault door. Bring me two old coins and I can match the date.

ask.text: Two old coins. Ivy at the bank sees them, and they turn up in the mine.

steps.hint: Bring Theo 2 Old Coins to date the vault.

lines.text: Coldy's key turns in the snowflake lock with a sound like ice cracking on a pond. The little room smells of cold stone and old paper.
The town's first bell rope. A bundle of seed packets, still good. And a letter: 'If you are reading this, you remembered. Ring the bell.'
Twenty-one years we forgot. I'll put the rope back on the bell myself.
Someone's been leaving fish on the end of my jetty. At night. Pike, gutted the way Tomas used to, badly, from the wrong end.
Nobody else does it that badly. Nobody. I sat up last night and nobody came. Marlowe sees the whole shore from the lamp; ask him?

steps.hint: Someone leaves pike on Finn's jetty at night. Ask Marlowe what he sees from the lighthouse.

lines.text: A thin fellow in grey rags. Walks the shore after dark, stands by Finn's boat, never knocks. Walks like he's carrying armour that isn't there any more.
He's lost, not bad. Lost people need a light to walk toward. Bring me two flasks of lamp oil and I'll hang lanterns down the jetty.

ask.text: Two flasks of lamp oil. Maple keeps it on the bottom shelf.

steps.hint: Bring Marlowe 2 Lamp Oil to light the jetty.

lines.text: Finn's boat is pulled up on the shore. Finn sits in it with a thin, tired man wrapped in a blanket, both of them looking at the lake.
He walked up the lanterns and sat in the boat. Didn't say anything for an hour. Then he said 'that's not the pike'.
He doesn't remember much of the Wastes. Good. He remembers the dock. He's home. Tomas is home.
A man in a shiny suit came to my kitchen door. Bellamy. He runs the diner on the avenue. He wants to buy my place, and he wasn't asking nicely.
I told him my kitchen is honest. Honest kitchens don't get sold, they get beaten. In a cook-off. Saturday.

steps.hint: Mama Rosa challenged a rival to a cook-off. Help her get ready.

lines.text: My fish stew won my mother a husband and my grandmother a war. Bring me three trout, fresh, and I'll win us a street.
Clean, mind. If I find a hook in one, you're washing pots.

ask.text: Three trout. The river, the lake, wherever they're biting. Fresh!

steps.hint: Bring Mama Rosa 3 Trout for the cook-off.

lines.text: The whole block crowds into Rosa's kitchen to taste. Bellamy takes one spoonful, puts the spoon down, and doesn't pick it up again.
He shook my hand. He's going to buy his bread from Posy now. Honest, see? Honest wins, it just needs a good stew behind it.
There's a table by the window with your name on it. Nobody else sits there. Not even me.
Don't laugh. I want to go back to school. Real school, with a bell and a desk and a teacher who's mean about spelling.
But the road past the old schoolhouse is where the collectors park. Nobody's sending their kid past that.

steps.hint: The Kid wants to go back to school. Ask Mayor Alder about making the road safe.

lines.text: A safe crossing by the schoolhouse? I'd sign that today. A fence, a gate, a lamp. The council has no money for it, of course. The council never has money.
Twenty planks and the town will build it. I'll stand there myself in the mornings if I have to.

ask.text: Twenty planks for the school fence. Saw them at the workshop from wood.

steps.hint: Bring Mayor Alder 20 Planks for the school crossing.

lines.text: The Kid shows up at the gate in a clean shirt, hair flattened with water, a satchel that's clearly new.
First day. The teacher's mean about spelling. It's the best.
You didn't have to do that. You did it anyway. That's the kind of crew I want to be in.
I was tidying a wire I'm not supposed to have. Found a folder I'm not supposed to see. M.'s private files.
Your name's in them, boss. Before you ever got to town. I'll need a day to read the rest without my hands shaking.

steps.hint: Specs found M.'s files with your name in them. Give Specs a day.

lines.text: M. picked you. The farm, the deed, the strawberry seeds. M. needed somebody who'd start out wanting to clean the city up and wouldn't notice what it cost them.
And there's more. Every one of the President's lieutenants has a page with the same word on it: 'gifted'. By the stone. Their tricks aren't tricks.

steps.hint: Specs read M.'s files: each lieutenant's power was a gift from the stone. Talk to Sal about it.

lines.text: So M. chose you, and the stone chose them. Doesn't matter who chose. What matters is what you do with the part that's yours.
You came here to take the gangs down, remember? Not to become one. You still can. I'd follow that version of you.
